chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: Memphis, the Conway brothers and a Tennessee tour with Don Dunbar
summary: The Conway brothers in Memphis, living near Beale Street, booking agent Dave Clark, and a Tennessee tour with a dancing, singing revue.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And there was also some other great saxophone players around Memphis. Two brothers, the Conway Brothers, one named Don, who played alto, and another one played tenor, his name was Buddy Conway. They were legendary through that part. And later on, I had the pleasure of working with Don with Doc Palamer's band. He came to Jackson, and he played in the saxophone section with us, you know. And he had his own band, yeah, out at a place called the Barn, a dance hall out in Memphis. And I was living right across from Handy Park on Beale Street. You know, that was nice, it being a legendary neighborhood, you know. Because I had heard about W.C. Handy, and it was nice to see these things as a kid. You know, you'd go to these places, and... We had a guy who became popular in the recording industry named Dave Clark, who later on because the booking agent for Don Dunbar's band, and we traveled all through Tennessee, different parts of Tennessee...
And I'll never forget, I think it was a little town named Marysville... Micki Gwynn(?), the singer with Don

Dunbar's band, who also played piano, lived in Marysville, Tennessee. And Earl Fatha Hines was playing in Nashville. And we drove 35 miles (this was a long way in those days) to go over to catch that band in Nashville. I spent a lot of time down through Tennessee also, and Arkansas, round through, with different people, doing different things, and learning, and watching and listening, you know.

Well, they had dancers and singers, a chorus line and everything, and singers... I mean, he was a tap dancer himself, Jimmy Gibbons, you know. And it was a really nice experience to add to my, heh, experiences, you know.
Yeah. Yeah, the Black theatre circuit around through the South. Yeah, we played theatres. Now and then we'd play a dance.
